transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, thank you for coming back in to see me. I have something important to discuss regarding your grandson's visit yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué pasó? What is it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: While we were giving the immunizations, a mistake was made. The vaccine we used was drawn up for a child in a heavier weight category. This means your grandson received a dose intended for an older, heavier child, rather than the dose based on his actual weight. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: He is so small. Why would you do that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an error in the preparation of the medication. The weight bands were confused. Just to be sure I am being clear, do you understand that he received more of the vaccine than he should have?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know. My baby. Is he okay? Is he going to be sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Based on the pharmacology of this specific vaccine, we do not expect any long-term complications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am scared. I am very scared. He was crying so much yesterday. What if it hurts his brain? What if he is sick now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Now, the clinical data shows that a single over-dose of this specific vaccine does not lead to those kinds of outcomes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not understand. He is my first grandchild. I cannot believe this happened. Why was this not checked?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The process for drawing the doses was not followed correctly. It is a systemic issue in how the labels are organized.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But he is just a baby. My heart is beating so fast. I feel like I cannot breathe. Look at me, I am shaking.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Let's look at the chart again so I can show you the actual milligrams he received versus what he should have had.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care about the numbers. My baby is in danger. Please tell me he is okay. I am terrified.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. The risk of a severe reaction is very low.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Low is not no. You told me he was safe. Now you say this. I cannot trust you. I am so afraid for him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have a set of protocols to monitor for any delayed reactions.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do I do? Do I take him to the hospital? Should I go now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on things. We can check back in a few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A few days? What happens tonight? What if he gets a fever? What if he stops eating? Tell me exactly what to do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just watch him. If you see something, give us a call.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Call who? The front desk? I cannot get through to anyone on the phone. I need a plan. I need to know if he is dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: He is not dying. We will see how it goes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot just wait and see. This is my baby. I am crying and you are just talking about charts. Do you even care?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we have to focus on the medical facts of the dosage.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot focus on facts when I am terrified. My daughter, tell him. Tell him we need a real answer.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Doctor, please. My mother is very upset. We need to know exactly what the next steps are. Is there a specialist we should see? What are the specific symptoms we are looking for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is no need for a specialist. We will just monitor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Monitor how? Do we come back? When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see. Maybe stay tuned for an email from our office regarding a follow-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? I need a date. I need a time. I cannot just wait for an email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have another patient waiting now, so we will have to wrap this up. We will reach out.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language at the end ('have another patient waiting', 'wrap this up') and shows defensive escalation by redirecting to facts while the patient is in acute distress.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, used lay language, and comprehension was checked twice ('Does that make sense so far?' and 'do you understand...').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'a mistake was made' and 'a systemic issue'.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand') repeatedly but never names specific emotions or engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague instructions ('we will see', 'stay tuned for an email', 'we will reach out') with no specific timeline or plan.
